data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The nocturnal UHI is fundamentally an anthropogenic heat flux phenomenon, and the cross-city gap scales directly with population density and energy consumption, particularly from nighttime HVAC and transportation emissions.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If cities with similar population densities show very different nocturnal UHI magnitudes due to different building geometry or vegetation, anthropogenic heat alone is insufficient.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the nocturnal UHI is stronger in summer than in winter despite higher winter heating energy use, the anthropogenic scaling is contradicted.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If reducing sky view factor increases UHI independently of population density, anthropogenic heat is not the single dominant mechanism.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Human activities inject heat directly into the urban atmosphere. The nocturnal gap is larger in cities with greater population density and higher energy use because the anthropogenic heat flux is proportional to energy consumption.
